AMZN.rationale: Amazon's franchise quality is among the highest in public markets: AWS reaccelerated to 28% YoY growth on a $150B revenue base (Q1 2026), advertising reached $70B+ TTM, and the $364B AWS backlog provides contracted demand visibility. Q1 2026 operating margin hit an all-time high of 13.1%, resolving the Q3 2025 operating-margin compression concern (9.7%) flagged by the quant report. Net income grew 77% YoY in Q1 2026. The balance sheet is essentially unlevered (D/E 0.149) with $35.5B quarterly OCF. However, at 36x P/E the stock sits in the upper quartile of its own 12-month range (28.2x–39.0x), the 2.8% earnings yield is 167bp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and the stock has already rallied +15.9% in one quarter. The $200B 2026 capex plan has collapsed FCF to $1.2B, and the October 2026 FTC antitrust trial plus EU regulatory tightening add structural cost overhang. The fundamental trajectory is genuinely strong, but the market has already re-rated the name aggressively, leaving limited margin of safety at current levels. No clear near-term catalyst beyond the Q2 earnings event to drive further re-rating from an already elevated multiple.
key_factors: Q1 2026 operating margin of 13.1% (all-time high) resolves Q3 2025 compression to 9.7%; operating income $23.9B on $181.5B revenue (+17% YoY)
AWS reaccelerated to 28% YoY growth ($37.6B Q1 2026 revenue), fastest in 15 quarters, with $364B backlog and deepening AI partnerships (Anthropic $25B, OpenAI $50B, Snowflake $6B)
P/E at 36.0x is in upper quartile of 12-month range (28.2x–39.0x); earnings yield 2.8% is 167bp below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47%, limiting further multiple expansion
Stock has already rallied +15.9% in ~63 trading days (from $218.94 to $253.79), pricing in much of the fundamental improvement
$200B 2026 capex plan collapsed trailing FCF to $1.2B from $25.9B (95% drop), creating monetization-gap risk if AI demand softens
FTC antitrust trial set for October 2026; EU proposing stricter cloud rules for government contracts — rising structural regulatory cost
Balance sheet is conservatively funded: D/E 0.149, total equity $369.6B, OCF $35.5B in Q3 2025
Berkshire Hathaway exited Amazon in Q1 2026 citing valuation, while Tepper/Ackman/Robbins increased stakes — mixed institutional signals

sources_cited.excerpt: Amazon reported Q1 2026 revenue of $181.5bn, up 17% year on year, with AWS revenue rising 28% to $37.6bn... operating margin of 13.1%, the highest operating margin in Amazon's history
Trailing free cash flow fell to $1.2 billion from $25.9 billion, a 95 percent drop. Operating cash flow rose 30 percent to $148.5 billion
AWS is 18% of Amazon's revenue but produces 57% of its profit... In 2025, AWS generated $128.7 billion in revenue with $45.6 billion in operating income
Advertising Services... Amazon's ad business pulled in $68.6 billion in 2025, making it larger than Amazon Prime revenue and one of the top three digital ad platforms in the United States
Snowflake announced a $6 billion multi-year commitment to AWS for Graviton compute and AI services
The most material risk cluster is now regulatory and political constraint on scale economics... FTC antitrust case trial date set for October 2026
Proposed [EU] rules could limit the ability of Amazon Web Services to compete for certain public-sector projects across the region
Custom Silicon as a Standalone Business... Graviton, Trainium, Inferentia, and Nitro now run at ~$20 billion annually with triple-digit growth
Berkshire Hathaway (Greg Abel) fully exited its Amazon position in Q1 2026, citing valuation; multiple billionaire investors (Tepper, Ackman, Robbins) significantly increased Amazon stakes
